labels.scripts: Script commands are called like this: ~/Applications/AI\ Hub\ Bar.app/Contents/MacOS/AIHubBar --sessions

facts.detail: Refresh projects in the open panel.
facts.name: ⌘R

facts.detail: Settings.
Quit AI Hub Bar.
facts.name: ⌘Q

facts.detail: With more than one profile enabled, a switcher sits at the top of the panel. Profiles are set up in Settings → “Profiles”; all settings can be saved to a .claudepult file (General → “Export Settings…”); double-clicking such a file imports it.
facts.name: Profiles

steps: Click ✦ in the menu bar to open the panel.
Create a profile: Settings → “Profiles” → “+” → “Assistant…”.
On the “Modules” page, keep only what you need — the rest turns off along with its background work.
In “Menu Bar”, pick what shows next to the icon.
topics.summary: AI Hub Bar keeps your AI limits, agent sessions and projects at hand — in the Mac menu bar, one click away.
topics.title: Getting started

facts.detail: Click — the panel. Red dot: some project is “red”. ✋ with a number: how many Claude sessions wait for an answer.
Share of the 5-hour session and the week used — as a number, ring or bar (Settings → “Menu Bar”): green below 50%, orange below 80%, red above.
facts.name: Next to the icon

facts.detail: Space, wide space, “·”, “|”, thin line, “/”, “›” and “New group” — as many times as you like. They show only when there’s something to show on both sides.
facts.name: Separators

facts.detail: Items between “New group” dividers are drawn on a shared rounded backing.
facts.name: Capsules by group

facts.detail: Switch the profile, and the menu bar changes too.
facts.name: Each profile has its own

steps: Open Settings → “Menu Bar”.
Click an item in “Order” to see its settings: number, ring or bar, threshold.
Drag a separator onto an item and it lands right after it. Without a mouse — “Further left” and “Further right”.
topics.summary: The icon and numbers next to the clock: limits, sessions waiting for an answer, project problems — whatever you put there.
topics.title: Menu Bar

facts.detail: The field at the top of the panel searches projects, sessions, commands and your own prompts. To open it from the keyboard, set a shortcut in “General”.
facts.name: Search

facts.detail: Clicking a block’s header collapses it; the panel remembers this.
facts.name: Collapse a block

facts.detail: Theme, glass background, text size, width and density — Settings → “Appearance”.
facts.name: Appearance

steps: Open Settings → “Panel”.
Drag a block onto another or click ⌃ / ⌄.
On the right you can see how the panel looks now.
topics.summary: The panel opens with a click on ✦: the current profile’s module blocks from top to bottom, plus search.
topics.title: Panel

facts.detail: A module that’s off doesn’t run in the background, isn’t shown in the panel or menu bar and sends no notifications. Its settings and place in profiles are kept.
facts.name: On/off switch

facts.detail: Chips on the module’s page: panel, menu bar, island, notifications, Telegram.
facts.name: Where to show

facts.detail: Settings → “Profiles” → “+” → “Assistant…”: a profile step by step — template, folder, stages, metrics, calendar, AI service, commands, permissions, panel blocks, menu bar, name. On the right — how it will look.
facts.name: Assistant

facts.detail: Settings → “Profiles” → “+”: “Developer (GitHub)”, “Video”, “Writing”, “Research”, “Social media”, “Custom”. Pick a folder — the profile is ready; everything else is changed in its settings.
facts.name: Add profile

steps: Settings → “Modules”: turn on a set (“AI only”, “Mac utilities”, “Everything”) or single tiles.
Clicking a tile opens the module’s page: the on/off switch, “Where to show” and all its settings.
topics.summary: A module is one feature of AI Hub Bar. A profile decides which modules show in the panel and in what order.
topics.title: Modules and profiles

facts.detail: The session with a countdown to the reset and a forecast from the last 30 min, the week, weeks per model, extra usage.
facts.name: “Limits” block

facts.detail: Codex, Copilot, Gemini, Cursor and API spend — in the same cards as Claude.
facts.name: Other AI

facts.detail: An estimate from Claude Code's logs: project shares and the most expensive session for the session, today, the week.
facts.name: Usage by project

facts.detail: Once per window at 50/80/95% (thresholds in Settings) and when the limit is back; optionally to Telegram too.
facts.name: Notifications

facts.detail: “Claude Limits” for the desktop: right-click the desktop → “Edit Widgets…” → AI Hub Bar. Small — the session ring, medium — session and week.
facts.name: Widget

facts.detail: If the session is more than 90 percent used, a background task asks: start now or after the reset.
facts.name: Background and limit

steps: Notification thresholds are on the “AI limits” page.
Other AIs are connected in “AI Services”: sign in to their CLI or add an API key.
topics.summary: How much is left of the 5-hour session and the week on your Claude subscription — and of other AIs’ limits.
topics.title: AI limits

facts.detail: Every session on this Mac — in Terminal, in the Claude app, in the background: project, worktree, task, duration, state (working, background, waiting, done, error, ended). Sessions waiting for an answer are highlighted and notified.
facts.name: List

facts.detail: “Allow” and “Deny” — in the notification, the session row, the island and, if turned on, Telegram. The first answer to arrive wins.
facts.name: Permissions

facts.detail: Bring this session's Terminal tab forward; for Claude app sessions open this session in Claude, otherwise the folder.
facts.name: Show

facts.detail: Where to run: a Terminal window (you can answer Claude) or claude -p without a window (allowed actions only, a time limit, the result as a notification and to Telegram). “Remember” or a default in Settings.
facts.name: Terminal / Background

facts.detail: ⌃⌥P in any app: the task, the project (the one in front, or the last one) and the agent — ⌘↩, and it runs in the background or in Terminal. The “Quick Prompt” module; the key is on its page.
facts.name: Quick Prompt

facts.detail: Background task: what Claude does, step by step.
facts.name: Log

facts.detail: Background task: stop now.
facts.name: Stop

facts.detail: Sessions are visible only with hooks installed in Settings (they are added to ~/.claude/settings.json; a copy is kept next to it).
facts.name: Hooks

facts.detail: Their sessions also show “running / waiting / done” when AI Hub Bar's hook is installed on their page under “AI Services”. Codex runs a new hook only after review: type /hooks in codex and trust it. Without the hook — only recent conversations, without a state.
facts.name: Codex and Copilot

steps: Install hooks: “Agent sessions” page → Hooks.
Answer permission requests right from the notification or the session row.
topics.summary: All Claude Code sessions on this Mac: what they’re doing, which are waiting for an answer, background tasks and the queue.
topics.title: Agent sessions

facts.detail: Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI — AI Hub Bar finds the installed ones (Settings → “AI Services”) and opens them in Terminal in the project folder: “Open in…” in a project's Claude block. Each has its own sign-in.
facts.name: Agents

facts.detail: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, DeepSeek, Mistral and any OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter). The key lives only in the macOS Keychain; “Check” spends no tokens.
facts.name: Models by API

facts.detail: Settings → “Profiles” → “Default service”: it runs the profile's command templates.
facts.name: Profile's service

steps: Settings → “AI Services”: a green dot means the service is found or set up.
topics.summary: Agents and models that AI Hub Bar finds and runs: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor and API models.
topics.title: AI Services

facts.detail: Health dot, branch, uncommitted files, open PRs (colour — CI), last activity.
facts.name: Row

facts.detail: Claude takes the first Next item and does it by the rules of ~/Projects/CLAUDE.md: branch, checks, PR, STATUS.
facts.name: Next step

facts.detail: Claude carries out your text by the same rules.
facts.name: Custom task…

facts.detail: Claude finishes the current work in the folder: checks, commit, push, PR, STATUS — no new code.
facts.name: Finish

facts.detail: If Claude already works in the project, a new task goes to a separate worktree .claude/worktrees/cb-… on a fresh branch from origin/main.
facts.name: Folder in use

facts.detail: Open the project folder or the repository.
facts.name: Terminal · Finder · GitHub

facts.detail: Settings → “Profiles” → “Source”: every folder inside the projects folder is a project (a video, an article, a topic).
facts.name: “Folders” source

facts.detail: The project card is plain text: “Stage: script”, “Deadline: 2026-11-05”, “Publish: 2026-11-05 18:00”, “Format: …”, “Main file: script.md”, “Platform: YouTube”. Edit it by hand any time.
facts.name: project.md

facts.detail: In an expanded project: the profile's commands and “Custom task”. The result is always a new file in the project folder. A model by API gets the main file's text; Claude works in the background with the profile's permissions (“files only” — no terminal, no internet); other agents open in Terminal with the task on the clipboard.
facts.name: Commands

facts.detail: Turn on “Compare”, pick 2–3 services and a command: the results land side by side (“hooks (Claude).md”, “hooks (OpenAI).md”) and open in the “Comparison” window.
facts.name: Compare

facts.detail: The profile's stages, comma-separated; a stage changes with a button in an expanded project. Words, duration, reading time and pages are counted on the main file (.md, .txt, .rtf, .docx).
facts.name: Stages and metrics

steps: Settings → “Profiles” → a profile → “Source”: the folder with your projects.
topics.summary: The profile’s projects: git repositories or work folders — status, PRs, stages and AI commands.
topics.title: Projects

facts.detail: Deadlines and publications from project.md, rows of content-plan.md — for profiles with the calendar on (Settings → “Profiles”).
facts.name: What's in it

facts.detail: A panel block: 7 days ahead, overdue in red; a click opens the project or file.
facts.name: Upcoming

facts.detail: Month or week. Drag an entry to another day — the date is rewritten in its file. Double-click a day — a new entry.
facts.name: “Calendar” window

facts.detail: On the “Upcoming” module page: how far ahead to remind you and whether to also send it to Telegram.
facts.name: Reminders

steps: Turn on the calendar in the profile — or use the “Turn on in the profile” button on the “Upcoming” tile.
topics.summary: Deadlines and publications from project cards and the content plan — a week ahead, and in the “Calendar” window.
topics.title: Upcoming and calendar

facts.detail: Report with an AI summary of the last 24 h to Telegram (1–3 min).
facts.name: Report now

facts.detail: Summary without AI for the last 24 h to Telegram.
facts.name: Quick summary

facts.detail: Open _daily-report/reports/latest.html.
facts.name: Latest report

facts.detail: Show what the build cleanup would delete, touching nothing.
facts.name: Cleanup: check

facts.detail: Delete builds and caches, reset simulators (with confirmation).
facts.name: Cleanup: run

topics.summary: _daily-report commands: report, quick summary, build cleanup.
topics.title: _daily-report reports

facts.detail: Left and right of the notch — a limit and sessions; exactly what is chosen on the module’s page.
facts.name: Ears

facts.detail: Hover over the notch to open a card with limits and what Claude is doing.
facts.name: Card

facts.detail: A permission request appears on the island with “Allow” and “Deny”; ⌃⌥Y / ⌃⌥N from the keyboard, if turned on.
facts.name: Requests

facts.detail: Drop a file on the island to open the profile’s AI commands for it.
facts.name: Drop a file on the island

facts.detail: On screens without a notch — a pill at the top center.
facts.name: Without a notch

steps: Turn on “Notch Island” on the “Modules” page.
topics.summary: A black island around the MacBook notch: the limit and sessions beside it; hover for a card with limits and what Claude is doing.
topics.title: Notch Island

facts.detail: A word typed in the wrong layout is fixed after you press Space, and the layout switches.
facts.name: Automatically

facts.detail: Converts the last word or undoes a wrong correction — and remembers the word.
facts.name: Double Shift

facts.detail: Converts the selected text to the other layout.
Needs “Accessibility” access: the module asks for it and shows where to turn it on.
facts.name: Access

steps: Turn on “Beta Builds” in “General”, then “Keyboard Layout” on the “Modules” page.
topics.summary: A word typed in the wrong keyboard layout is retyped in the right one by itself, and the layout switches. Double Shift converts the last word, ⌥⇧ the selected text. The language is in the menu bar.
topics.title: Keyboard Layout

facts.detail: Processor, memory, disk, network, battery and the hungriest apps; alerts about load, memory, space and charge.
facts.name: Mac Resources

facts.detail: The Mac stays awake while Claude works, for a while, on power or with a display connected, or while chosen apps are open.
facts.name: Keep Awake

facts.detail: Dark Mode, desktop icons, locking and turning off the display, ejecting disks, the Trash — in one click.
facts.name: Quick Toggles

facts.detail: Recent copies: search, pin, back to the clipboard in one click. Passwords from password managers are not recorded.
facts.name: Clipboard History

facts.detail: Markdown notes right in the panel: tabs over plain .md files in a folder any editor can open.
facts.name: Notes

facts.detail: Your own buttons: a script in the background or in Terminal, a macOS «Shortcuts» shortcut, a link, file, folder or app. Each can have its own keyboard shortcut.
facts.name: Quick Commands

topics.summary: Mac resources, “Keep Awake”, quick toggles, clipboard history, notes and your own commands — each one turns on separately.
topics.title: Mac utilities

facts.detail: Each module’s page has “How often to notify”: every time, at most once per 15 min, per hour, per day, or never.
facts.name: How often

facts.detail: The bot is in “General” → Telegram. What to forward is set with the “Telegram” chip on the module’s page.
facts.name: Telegram

facts.detail: Claude’s permission requests can be allowed or denied with buttons in Telegram — a separate bot, on the “Agent sessions” page.
facts.name: Answers from Telegram

facts.detail: Takes you to the session, PR, log or report.
facts.name: Clicking a notification

topics.summary: What comes as a macOS notification and to Telegram, and how often.
topics.title: Notifications and Telegram
